response.sql: WITH order_averages AS (SELECT o.orderspivot, oe.ordersmark, o.timespan, AVG(oe.fillcount) AS order_avg_fill FROM orderexecutions AS oe JOIN orders AS o ON oe.ordersmark = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.orderspivot, oe.ordersmark, o.timespan), ranked AS (SELECT ordersmark, timespan, order_avg_fill, AVG(order_avg_fill) OVER (PARTITION BY timespan) AS tif_avg_fill, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY timespan ORDER BY order_avg_fill DESC NULLS LAST) AS fill_rank FROM order_averages) SELECT ordersmark, timespan, order_avg_fill, order_avg_fill - tif_avg_fill AS above_tif_avg_fill, fill_rank FROM ranked WHERE order_avg_fill > tif_avg_fill AND fill_rank <= 3

assumptions.assumption: The time-in-force average is the average of the per-order averages, so each matched order has equal weight.

alternatives.interpretation: The time-in-force average is taken across all matched execution fillcounts, so orders with more nonnull fills have more weight.
alternatives.sql: WITH matched AS (SELECT o.orderspivot, oe.ordersmark, o.timespan, oe.fillcount FROM orderexecutions AS oe JOIN orders AS o ON oe.ordersmark = o.recordvault), order_averages AS (SELECT orderspivot, ordersmark, timespan, AVG(fillcount) AS order_avg_fill FROM matched GROUP BY orderspivot, ordersmark, timespan), tif_averages AS (SELECT timespan, AVG(fillcount) AS tif_avg_fill FROM matched GROUP BY timespan), ranked AS (SELECT oa.ordersmark, oa.timespan, oa.order_avg_fill, ta.tif_avg_fill, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY oa.timespan ORDER BY oa.order_avg_fill DESC NULLS LAST) AS fill_rank FROM order_averages AS oa JOIN tif_averages AS ta ON oa.timespan IS NOT DISTINCT FROM ta.timespan) SELECT ordersmark, timespan, order_avg_fill, order_avg_fill - tif_avg_fill AS above_tif_avg_fill, fill_rank FROM ranked WHERE order_avg_fill > tif_avg_fill AND fill_rank <= 3
